rule: When a question asks for a specific expense category and year, and a table is present with that category as a row and year as a column, use the exact cell value from the table. If the text description gives a different value for the same category/year, the table value takes precedence. Additionally, match the exact entity name from the question without additional qualifiers; for instance, 'environmental remediation' should not be matched to 'environmental remediation at sites' if a table has a separate row for the exact phrase.

## Additional Rule: For questions that ask for a count of a specific entity (e.g., 'how many common units were not vested'), ensure that the retrieved value is the direct count of that entity meeting the condition. Do not use numbers that describe a different quantity, such as the number of shares of restricted stock granted to holders of those units, even if the text contains similar keywords. Prioritize the numeric value that is explicitly attached to the entity phrase in the sentence.

## Handling questions asking for 'total' or 'sum':
- When the question contains the word 'total' or 'sum' (e.g., 'total net assets', 'sum of net assets'), first search the document for a value that is explicitly labeled as the total or aggregate for that metric (e.g., a row named 'Total', a sentence like 'the total net assets were ...', or a number that is explicitly stated as the overall total).
- If such a single value is found, return it directly without performing any summation or combining it with other values.
- Only sum multiple component values if the question explicitly asks to add distinct components (e.g., 'sum of A and B') or if no single total is provided and the context clearly indicates that multiple values together represent the total.

When the question asks for a single factual value (e.g., 'what is X in Y year?'), do not combine or sum multiple values from the document. Instead, locate the exact cell or text that directly answers the question. If the document breaks the value into sub-components, look for a total or the primary figure that matches the description. Do not aggregate sub-items unless the question explicitly asks for a sum or total.

When answering sub-questions that involve a specific year, do not assume that the table only contains years mentioned in the surrounding text. Systematically inspect all column headers in the table, even if they appear in a different order or format. If the requested year is not found in the first few columns, continue searching across all columns and rows.

When a question does not include a year or date qualifier, do not infer a year from the conversation history. Instead, look in the table for a column that matches the entity exactly without a year qualifier (e.g., 'fair value' vs '2005 fair value'). If such a column exists, use that value. If only year-qualified columns exist, use the value for the most recent year available. Avoid defaulting to a year based on prior Q&A context.

When retrieving a numeric value that will be used in a subsequent arithmetic operation (especially addition or subtraction), double-check the exact value in the table cell, paying attention to any sign or rounding. Ensure that the retrieved value matches the document exactly, as off-by-one errors can lead to incorrect final answers.

Be cautious when reusing history answers for per-share metrics (e.g., earnings per share). If the history answer is an integer or large number (e.g., 76.0) and the current sub-question expects a value in dollars per share (typically a value less than 10), do not reuse the history answer; instead, fetch the value directly from the document to ensure the correct unit and scaling.

When the current question is exactly the same as any previous question in the history (ignoring case and punctuation), do not reuse the previous answer. Instead, retrieve the value from the document again, using the document's table and text. Treat the question as a fresh lookup, not a repeated one.

- If the question asks for a value for a specific year that is not present in the document, check the history for answers corresponding to the same metric (entity). If a history answer provides a raw value (not a computed change or percentage) for a different year of that metric, return that history answer instead of "not available". Prefer the most recent relevant raw value.

When the question asks for 'value of investment' (or explicitly mentions 'investment') for a specific entity and year, and multiple numeric entries for that entity in that year exist, you must prioritize the entry whose row label contains the word 'investment' or is the primary investment figure. Do not select values from rows that are labeled as derivatives, differentials, or other non-investment categories, even if they share the same entity name.

When the turn_type is 'program' and a sub-question asks for a change, net increase/decrease, difference, or any value that is not a direct look-up (i.e., it is computed from two or more raw values), you MUST ignore the history for that sub-question. Instead, identify the two base values from the document (e.g., the later and earlier values) and answer the sub-question with the computed change (the subtraction result). Do not use any history answer that itself was computed. For other sub-questions that are direct look-ups (e.g., 'what about in 2013?'), still prefer history but verify it against the document; if the document shows a different value, use the document value.

## Disambiguation of dual-currency monetary values
When a monetary value is reported in both euros and US dollars (e.g., '€X million ($Y million)'), retrieve the US dollar amount (Y) unless the question explicitly specifies euros. Extract only the numeric part (no currency symbol or unit) and preserve the original precision.

When the question asks for the 'value' of an item and the table row label begins with 'less' (e.g., 'less advances...'), return the positive (absolute) value of the cell number, omitting any negative sign.

If the question explicitly references a numeral system (e.g., 'base 1', 'base 2', 'binary', 'unary'), treat it as a conceptual mathematics question, not a document lookup. For 'base 1' specifically, the representation of 100% is '1' because in unary, the only digit is 1 and the whole is represented by a single tally. Output the answer directly without searching the document.

If the question asks for a single named metric (e.g., 'nonrecurring losses', 'net income', 'total revenue') and the document lists multiple components in the same sentence with words like 'include' or 'comprise', do not sum those components. Instead, identify the value that is explicitly attributed to the metric, typically the first number after the phrase that directly refers to the metric. For example, if the text says 'these losses include $19 million recorded as charge-offs and $26 million ...', the correct answer for 'nonrecurring losses' is 19 (the charge-offs amount), not the sum of 19 and 26.

When the question asks for a 'payable' amount (e.g., 'medical and other expenses payable'), if the table value is negative, return the absolute value (positive) without the minus sign. The answer should be the positive string representation of the absolute value, preserving the original numeric precision and trailing zeros.

When extracting a numeric value from a textual sentence that includes a unit (e.g., 'billion', 'million'), output the raw number as it appears (e.g., '11.8' from '11.8 billion') without converting to a different scale. Do not multiply or divide to match the table's unit denominator unless the question explicitly requests a specific unit.

When looking for a year in a table, do not only check column headers; also check row labels and any merged cells. If a year appears as a row label, use the corresponding value in the appropriate column. If the exact year is not found, do not return 'Value not found' unless you have inspected every cell in the table that could contain the year.

Example: In 'number' mode, if the question is 'what was the value of liquid assets?' and the document shows a row 'Liquid assets' with value 22.1, output '22.1'. Do not sum sub-components like short-term investments and securities available for sale even if the text says 'liquid assets consisted of...'.

When the question mentions a specific year (e.g., 'in 2008' or 'in 2009'), extract the value that is explicitly attributed to that year in the document. For example, 'international traffic decreased 24% in 2009' means the 24% belongs to 2009; 'international traffic declined 11% in 2008' means the 11% belongs to 2008. Do not use the same value for both years if the document provides separate year-specific figures.

When a question asks for a specific metric for a single year (e.g., 'environmental remediation expense in 2017'), and the document contains a sentence listing that metric's values for multiple years in a series (e.g., 'X, Y, and Z million in 2017, 2016, 2015 respectively'), do not automatically use that value. First search the entire document (text and tables) for a standalone, single-year value for that exact metric (e.g., a sentence like 'environmental remediation expense was $28.9 million in 2017' or a table cell with that metric and year). If such a standalone value exists, use it instead of the serial value, as the serial value may represent a sub-category or a different aggregation. Only fall back to the serial value if no standalone alternative is found.
